s1.title: Git at any scale
s1.summary: This technical article from Cursor describes the architecture of its Origin Git-hosting platform and Continuity storage system. It examines the scalability, availability, consistency, replication, routing, and compaction challenges of hosting Git repositories, comparing filesystem, object-level, and Spokes-style replication with a WAL-backed design using S3-compatible storage and local NVMe repositories.

s2.title: Stretching Spokes
s2.summary: This is a technical architecture article about GitHub’s Spokes system for replicating Git repositories across geographically distant datacenters, including GitHub Enterprise. It discusses reducing replication latency and round trips, transactional Git reference updates, checksum-based consistency verification, prioritization of user updates, and routing reads to nearby synchronized replicas.

s3.title: Building resilience in Spokes
s3.summary: This is a technical architecture document about GitHub’s Spokes replication system, formerly called DGit, which stores repositories, wikis, and gists. It discusses availability and durability trade-offs, replica placement, majority-based write commits and conflict handling, failure detection and routing, automated repair, and procedures for safely rebooting or retiring servers.

s4.title: Scalar philosophy
s4.summary: This document describes Scalar, Microsoft’s Git performance configuration tool, and its relationship to custom Git builds and upstream Git features. It discusses decisions around repository maintenance, partial clone and GVFS protocol use, sparse checkout, file-system monitoring, data-structure updates, compression, and repository layout to improve performance for large repositories.

s5.title: Introducing Scalar
s5.summary: This technical announcement from Microsoft introduces Scalar, a .NET tool for improving Git performance in very large repositories. It discusses design decisions around limiting working-tree files with sparse checkout, reducing object transfer through GVFS/partial clone, and detecting changes with filesystem monitoring. It also describes incremental background maintenance for fetching, commit graphs, loose objects, and pack files.
